This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Cleveland, Ohio, I'm Dale Willman.
A federal judge has dismissed President Trump's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal
As NPR's Steven Bassaha reports, it involved a birthday card Trump allegedly sent to late
convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The letter included a drawing of a naked woman
and what appeared to be the president's signature. The journal reported this in July last year.
Trump denied anything to do with the letter and called the journal's story fake and sued for at
least $10 billion in damages. The federal judge dismissed the lawsuit, declining to rule on whether
the actual reporting was false and saying the president had failed to show the journal had acted
with actual malice. This is the second time Trump has tried to sue the Wall Street Journal over this
reporting. The latest case was dismissed with prejudice, preventing Trump from filing another
lawsuit. Steven Bassaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama. The Supreme Court hears arguments
this week in a case that pits the Catholic Church against taxpayer funded school programs for all
four year olds in Colorado, NPR's Nina Totenberg reports. The first line of the Bill of Rights
says Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion or prohibiting the free
exercise of religion. But what happens when these two provisions clash? In this week's case,
the question is whether a taxpayer funded program that provides pre-k schooling for all four year
olds in the state must include a religious group, in this case, the Catholic archdiocese of Denver,
which bars the children of gay and trans parents from the pre-k program. If the church prevails,
the next target is likely to be charter schools. Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
The FBI says North Korean hackers are responsible for the biggest cryptocurrency heist in history.
Binance lost about $6.3 billion this week. The bureau said Saturday that the attack was
tied to malicious activity by an entity known as the Traitor Traitor. That's the same group that
was behind a one and a half billion dollar hack last year. The G20 meeting has ended and world
leaders failed to reach consensus on a number of global security issues, including the war in
Ukraine. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says a broad discussion on world supply chains
involved the freedom of navigation in the Black Sea, where Ukraine ships its grain.
Both Turkey and India have come to the table with some ideas about how we can get grain shipments
moving because this is threatening the world of food security and some energy security as well.
In the case of the straits, it's more challenging, of course, because many countries around the world
don't have the ability to project power in the region. President Trump says Brazilian Senator
Flavia Bolsonaro can stay in the U.S. as long as he wants. Bolsonaro left Brazil under secrecy
after recently losing the country's presidential election to leftist president Luis Inacío Lula
de Silva. He arrived in Miami. On Wednesday, he is under investigation in Brazil for corruption.
You're listening to NPR News.
In Kenya, a youth employment program devoted to climate change is preparing for a potential
record El Niño season. As NPR's Dury Buskerin reports, they're called the Green Army.
Some 4,000 workers have fanned out across Nairobi, clearing debris from streams and widening drainage
systems. More than 100 canyons died during flash floods in March, and residents are pressuring
the government to do more. Green Army Supervisor Tobias Sifuna says this effort works because
debris can clog the city's waterways during heavy rains. So we are cleaning drainages,
we are unclogging, that when the rains come, they are able to allow the smooth flow of the
wastewater and the stormwater. Teams are also dismantling unauthorized structures that were
set up by the community. Dury Buskerin, NPR News. U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham says
his government will consider apologizing for the first time for its role in the transatlantic
slave trade, but he rejects calls for the country to pay reparations. He made his comments to the
Guardian newspaper Friday. They came as the U.K. looks to strengthen its relations with nations
in Africa and the Caribbean. Burnham says Britain needs to acknowledge its complicated
history in order to protect the Commonwealth. In just their second season of play, the Golden
State Valkyries won the WNBA championship Saturday night by beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63.
It was Game 7 of the Best of Seven series. Gabby Williams finished with 30 points in the win,
including her team's last 11 points of the third quarter. Jordan Canada scored 18 points for the
dream. I'm Dale Willman, NPR News. This message comes from Odoo. Running a
